--- title: "Letter knowledge" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · LEC_LETRAS" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (C · Oral reading fluency; quality class A). Generated on November 27, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea LEC_LETRAS`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Conocimiento de letras*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/LEC_LETRAS.html). ::: **In one sentence.** Letter knowledge, from age 4 to 6 (10,527 administrations in 5 cohorts; 3 forms). Stability across time points ρ = .65. AUC .69–.83 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 1887 535 5431 67 | | Battery | LEEDUCA | | Format | reading aloud | | Items | 28 (535); 52 (67) according to the platform | | Task family | C · Oral reading fluency | | Score | Correct responses per minute | | Instructions (platform) | The child says the name or the sound of the 26 letters presented one by one in capital and lowercase on the screen. If the child says a wrong name or delays more than 5ss, the answer is scored as error. | ## How it is programmed on the platform The platform is the reference: what the activity actually presents is what is measured. Configuration read from the activity itself on 22/10/2026 (without modifying it). Cell contents are in Spanish. | Code|Name on the platform |Presentation | Test items| Practice items|Example items |Time limit |Order |Scoring | Age.term (label 3)| |----:|:--------------------|:------------------------------------------------|----------:|--------------:|:-------------|:-------------|:---------|:------------------------------|-----------------------:| | 535|Letras |Una letra por pantalla (mayúsculas) | 28| 0|A, B |5 s por letra |aleatorio |Aciertos y tiempo (eficiencia) | 4.2, 4.3, 5.1, 5.2, 5.3| | 67|Letras |Una letra por pantalla (minúsculas y mayúsculas) | 52| 0|a, B |60 s en total |aleatorio |Aciertos y tiempo (eficiencia) | 5.1, 5.2, 5.3, 6.1, 6.2| **Differences from the dictionary or the instructions (in Spanish):** - **535.** 28 ítems (solo mayúsculas, con K, LL y Ñ) y límite de 5 s por letra; no es intercambiable con la 67 (52 letras, 60 s). - **67.** 52 ítems (26 minúsculas + 26 mayúsculas, sin k ni ñ) con límite de 60 s: la puntuación depende de cuántas letras se presentan. El catálogo de tareas agrupa 67 y 535 con 52 ítems, pero 535 tiene 28 (solo mayúsculas, con K, LL y Ñ, sin límite total). *Age.term: provisional reading of the activity's label 3 (3rd digit = age, 4th = term; 0 = annual), to be confirmed with the engineer.* **How it looks on the platform** (first item or example; 2026 screenshot; the interface is in Spanish). ::: {layout-ncol=2} ![535 · Letras](../../figuras/plataforma/535.jpg){.lightbox fig-alt="Screenshot of activity 535"} ![67 · Letras](../../figuras/plataforma/67.jpg){.lightbox fig-alt="Screenshot of activity 67"} ::: ## Theoretical framework Letter knowledge is the ability to recognize each grapheme and associate it with its name or sound. It is the gateway to the **alphabetic principle**. The platform measures it in two ways: naming letters, and choosing the letter with which the name of a picture begins, which also requires isolating the first sound. **What the evidence says.** Together with phonological awareness and rapid naming, it is one of the three major predictors of reading. Its weight is similar in English, Spanish and Czech [@caravolas2013growth]. In Spanish, letter knowledge is the best predictor of simple syllable reading; phonological awareness weighs more for complex syllables [@martinez2020silabica]. The full review of the evidence is in the [letter knowledge pilot task sheet](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/LET.html) (*in Spanish*). **What our data show.** Both tasks have very high internal consistency (α = .90 and .97). Letter naming is stable between terms (ρ = .73) and predicts low Woodcock-Muñoz fluency years later with a median AUC of .71. As a skill with a ceiling, it discriminates mainly at ages 4 and 5. ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Form| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| At those time points this task cannot be used to grade difficulty. These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_LEC_LETRAS_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ### Forms: can they be pooled? LEEDUCA battery) assesses alphabetic knowledge. The child reads aloud the stimuli shown on the screen and the examiner records each correct response or error. It comprises 52 items. The time limit is 60 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013 and 2014 cohorts it was administered in 17 sessions, from 4 to 6 years of age. The main outcome is the efficiency (correct responses per unit of time). In our data (2021 analyses), internal consistency was α = .97 (N = 2,127, 52 items). Stability across successive administrations (median interval of 4 months) was ρ = .76 (median of 12 session pairs; range -0.06–.92). Because the task is timed, α tends to overestimate reliability; stability across administrations is the preferred estimate. Stability across time points was ρ = .40–.93. Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .57–.65. ## Pending issues - Extreme value at 5.2 (form 1887), 5.3 (form 535): the maximum or minimum is more than 2 SD away from P99 or P1. Check in the raw data (possible timing or recording error). - Floor effect in the norms at 6.1 (form 1887): at least 10% of children have the worst possible score, so P10 does not exist. At those time points the "severe" and "very severe" levels must not be assigned with this task (study M3). - The task has 3 forms; in 5 of 7 comparisons they have different scales. Norms are given by form (see "Forms"). - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
